The workshop stood at the end of the lane, and it had stood there long
enough that no one in the town could remember it being built.

Its windows were small and its door was low, and above the door hung a
sign so faded that only the painter could have said what it once showed.

Inside, the clockmaker kept his silence and his tools, and asked nothing
of the street beyond the light it let him borrow in the mornings.

When he died the workshop was locked, and the key was lost, and the lane
grew quiet in a way it had not been quiet before.
